blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Practical tax planning at the intermediate level is about making decisions slightly earlier than the deadline forces you to. A major investment deserves a conversation with the tax advisor before it is signed, not after it is booked. A new hire's contract structure can be shaped before the first payslip, not corrected three months later. A change in the company's legal structure is sometimes a tax opportunity — but only if you discuss it with a year's notice, not a month's.

None of this is aggressive or dishonest. Good tax planning uses the rules exactly as they are written. It simply takes advantage of the fact that the same transaction, handled slightly differently, can carry a different tax weight — and the difference is sometimes significant.

You should always bring tax into the conversation at the planning stage. By the time a deal has been signed, most of the tax opportunities have already passed quietly out the door.

items.q: According to the text, what is practical tax planning mainly about?
options: Rewriting the tax rules in your favour
Delaying every transaction until the deadline
Making decisions slightly earlier than the deadline forces you to
Paying less than the law requires
items.why: "about making decisions slightly earlier than the deadline forces you to".

items.q: How does the text describe good tax planning?
options: Neither aggressive nor dishonest — it uses the rules as written
items.why: "None of this is aggressive or dishonest. Good tax planning uses the rules exactly as they are written."

items.q: What does the text say about a new hire's contract structure?
options: It can be shaped before the first payslip
It has no effect on tax
It cannot be changed once agreed
It should be corrected three months later
items.why: "can be shaped before the first payslip, not corrected three months later."

items.q: The phrase "passed quietly out the door" suggests that, once a deal is signed, the tax opportunities…
options: must be reported to the government
items.why: Inferência: "quietly" indica que as oportunidades somem sem alarde — perdidas sem que ninguém perceba.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The same transaction can carry a different tax weight depending on how it is handled
Tax should be discussed at the planning stage
Calling the advisor after the deal is signed is the smart way to save tax
Timing is central to good tax planning
items.why: Inferência: todo o texto defende trazer o tema ANTES da assinatura; chamar o consultor depois é justamente o erro.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie conversando com o cliente antes da assinatura. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thanks for bringing me in early on this one. Six weeks before you sign is exactly the right moment — if you'd called me the day after, half of what I'm about to say would already be off the table.

So here's where I've landed. The investment itself is sound; I'm not questioning that. But the way the contract is structured, everything lands in a single tax year, and that pushes you into a much heavier bracket than you need to be in.

If we split the payment across two years — same total, same counterparty, same deal — the weight drops noticeably. We're not hiding anything; we're just using a rule that's sitting right there in the code. The government wrote it; we're allowed to use it.

My recommendation is that you ought to hold off on signing for another week. Let me draft the revised structure, walk your CFO through it, and then you sign with your eyes open. Believe me, this is the cheap part of the process. The expensive mistakes all happen after the ink is dry.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why does Sophie say the timing is right?
options: She was brought in six weeks before signing
The tax year has just ended
The deal has already been signed
The CFO asked her to wait
items.why: "Six weeks before you sign is exactly the right moment."

items.q: What is the problem with the way the contract is currently structured?
options: The total amount is too high
Everything lands in a single tax year, pushing the client into a heavier bracket
items.why: "everything lands in a single tax year, and that pushes you into a much heavier bracket."

items.q: What does Sophie recommend the client do?
options: Hold off on signing for another week
Sign immediately to lock in the price
items.why: "you ought to hold off on signing for another week."

items.q: When Sophie says "we're just using a rule that's sitting right there in the code," she is emphasising that the approach is…
options: something to keep from the CFO
a loophole that might be closed
items.why: Inferência: ela reforça que a regra foi escrita pelo governo e está no código — ou seja, é plenamente legal.

items.q: What does Sophie mean by "The expensive mistakes all happen after the ink is dry"?
options: The client should use a cheaper pen
The CFO makes most of the mistakes
Signing documents costs a lot of money
Once the deal is signed, correcting tax problems is far costlier
items.why: Inferência: depois da assinatura as oportunidades já passaram; consertar depois sai caro.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We should talk to the accountant at the planning stage." The planning stage is…
options: the moment after the deal is closed
the early phase, before decisions are locked in
items.why: Planning stage = fase de planejamento, quando as decisões ainda podem ser moldadas.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Filing after the ___ means paying penalties on top of the tax."
items.why: Deadline = prazo; perdê-lo gera multas.

items.q: "She restructured the payment to reduce the tax weight." Tax weight refers to…
options: the number of forms to complete
the size of the accounting department
the overall tax burden the transaction carries
items.why: Tax weight = carga tributária, o peso do imposto sobre a operação.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "They shaped the new hire's ___ before the first payment went out."
items.why: Contract structure = estrutura contratual, definida antes do primeiro holerite.

items.q: "Changing the company's legal structure can be a tax opportunity." Legal structure means…
options: the wording of a single contract
the legal form the company takes (its incorporation and status)
the office building and its layout
items.why: Legal structure = estrutura jurídica: a forma legal/constituição da empresa.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas sobre planejamento tributário. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the revised structure." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "Let's hold off on signing until the advisor reviews it." To hold off on means to…
options: delay or wait before doing something
items.why: Hold off on = adiar, esperar antes de agir.

items.q: "Splitting the payment across two years could bring down the tax bill." To bring down means to…
items.why: Bring down = reduzir, baixar (o valor).

items.q: "Good planning helps you take advantage of the rules as they're written." To take advantage of means to…
items.why: Take advantage of = aproveitar, fazer bom uso de algo (aqui, sem conotação negativa).

items.q: "Once the deal is closed, those savings slip through your fingers." This means the savings…
options: are lost before you can secure them
items.why: Slip through your fingers = escapar, perder-se antes que você consiga garantir.
